plaintext.source: A contemporary hand glossed every cipher run and the code numbers 9, 10, 11, 24, 72, 73 above the line.

transcription.notes: 8 runs (G01-G08) and the whole clear text (f131/transcription.md), transcribed 2 Oct 2026. docs/_check_profile.py --measure gives 140 tokens including the 8 run labels: 130 cipher signs + 1 struck sign + 1 code number inside a run. A further 7 bare code numbers stand in the clear text.

system.summary: Clear letter with inserted runs in a homophonic, partly polyphonic letter-and-figure substitution (signs of one character or 1+character), plus bare code numbers for persons and places.

conditions.human_role: Target chosen by the user from the catalogue; no hand help.

solution.what: Gallica ark of fr. 3976 (btv1b9060548h) found in gallica_sweep; f. 62 = canvas 111 by pencil foliation; BnF notice gives piece 30, 29 April 1588, letter with cipher, no decipherment.
First transcription of the 19 cipher runs from full-resolution crops (runs_first_pass.txt).
Tomokiyo Nevers keys nos. 16, 11, 10, 18 and the alphabet on fr. 3995 canvas 45 applied to run R01: no French.
Ciphertext-only homophonic anneals (solve.py, solve2.py, solve3.py; letter, null-i and i-as-space variants, unigram penalty, 8 restarts of 200k steps): e/n/t collapse, no French.
Symbol ciphers of ff. 56 and 60 (with decipherments) checked: different system.
f. 131 (4 June 1588, same hand) has interlinear decipherments; aligning 'conte de Brissac' and 'quelques mutins d'entr'eux' showed signs are one character or 1+character and gave ~15 values.
Runs read one by one with the partial key and clear context (Villeroy, Bellievre, du royaume, leur entreprise a failly, chancellier et d'O, ligueurs), extending the key each time.
Second zoomed pass: z read as 2, curly d as 8, g as 9 in several runs; readings re-derived.
All 19 runs read as French in context; 350/353 plaintext letters read (reading.tsv), name in R01 and one word in R18 tentative.
f. 131r fetched through Gallica IIIF (canvas 221, full/full native); canvas 222 is f. 132 and blank, so the letter is one page.
Whole clear text and all 8 cipher runs of f. 131r transcribed at native resolution (f131/transcription.md, f131/ciphertext.txt); 22 Sept work had used only the glosses of G01, G02, G04.

Key of key.md + the r3708 additions applied by f131/decode.py (DP alignment against the reading): all 130 signs fit; the first-candidate blind decode already gives 'quelques mbtipf dentreeblx', 'conte de bgisfac', 'que sil perisfoit', 'marquifat de salbce'.

Every run compared with its interlinear gloss: all 8 agree (conte de Brissac; a esté tué et que d'Elbeuf est au fort Saincte Caterine; que s'il perissoit; perist avec luy; Savoie s'arme; Roy; marquisat de Saluce). The 22 Sept gloss reading 'que s'il pouvoit' corrected to 'que s'il perissoit' from the cipher (14 = r).
First segmentation of G04 as '1n'=i, '1e'=i (key.md signs) left 'quesi' without l and 'perissoi' without t.

Re-segmented with a bare 1 = i followed by n = l and e (epsilon) = t: G04 'que s'il perissoit' and 'Caterine' (G03) read in full; the same split reads f. 62 'failly' (4 2 1 n o y), 'avoit' (k 1 e) and 'remueroit' (17 1 e) with no change of reading. key.md's 1n and 1e are therefore bare 1 + n / e, not two-character signs.

Code glosses on f. 131: 9 = Guise ('guis'), 10 = Espernon, 11 = le Roy, 24 = Nevers, 72 = Savoie, 73 = ambassadeur (Savoy's); 9 and 72/73 new from the glosses. New sign value b = y (G07 'Roy', single occurrence, glossed).
fr-1600-letters LM on the runs as read: -1.56 per char (real text -1.1 to -1.8); 33/33 words read as French, 30/33 in the fr-henri4 corpus vocabulary (Caterine, perissoit, perist are not).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 464 tokens, 44 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.141 per letter; random keys -5.261 (z 8.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.016 (mean -3.115, z 15.5); annealer on the real text -2.599. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.875; polyphony 0.06; 13 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.599

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was built from the interlinear decipherments on f. 131 of the same volume (BnF fr. 3976), a 4 June 1588 letter by the same informant in the same cipher ('conte de Brissac', 'quelques mutins d'entr'eux'), then extended run by run from the clear context of f. 62.
